disclaimer: Typical ranges for ordinary grades, not a setting to type in blindly. The number on the spool and the printer's filament profile win. Specialty blends (silk, high-flow, carbon fiber) can sit outside these ranges.

materials.name: PLA
materials.chamber_note: Keep it cool. Lid or door open on an enclosed printer. Heat creep starts when the box gets hot.
materials.good_for: First prints, models, and indoor parts that will not get hot.
materials.watch_outs: Softens around a hot car or a sunny windowsill. Strings if it is wet or too hot.

materials.name: PETG
materials.chamber_note: Ambient is fine. A closed hot box is not required.
materials.good_for: Clips, brackets, and parts that need to be tougher than PLA.
materials.watch_outs: Strings. Sticks hard to smooth PEI, so use glue or a textured plate as a release layer.

materials.name: TPU
materials.chamber_note: Ambient. The limit is the extruder, not the chamber.
materials.good_for: Grips, bumpers, and hinges. 95A is a common firm grade.
materials.watch_outs: Print slowly. Soft grades buckle in the extruder and are often banned from AMS/CFS units. Check the spool.

materials.name: ABS
materials.chamber_note: Warm air, roughly 40–60 °C, passive or heated. Drafts lift corners.
materials.good_for: Functional parts that see more heat than PLA, when you can enclose and ventilate.
materials.watch_outs: Warps. Gives off styrene. Do not print it in a bedroom. See Safety.

materials.name: ASA
materials.chamber_note: Same idea as ABS: warm, still air.
materials.good_for: Outdoor parts. It handles sunlight better than ABS.
materials.watch_outs: Warps like ABS and needs the same ventilation. Acetone smoothing works, outdoors.

materials.name: PA / nylon
materials.chamber_note: Warm to hot, about 40–60 °C or more. PA-CF wants a hardened nozzle.
materials.good_for: Strong, tough parts that see heat and impact.
materials.watch_outs: Extremely hygroscopic. Dry it before every print and keep it in a dry box. Carbon fiber wears brass nozzles.

materials.name: PC
materials.chamber_note: Hot, about 50–60 °C or more. The bed alone is often not enough.
materials.good_for: Parts that must stay stiff when hot.
materials.watch_outs: Warps badly. Use glue, a brim, slow first layers, and no drafts.
